description: We are a team of enthusiastic and innovative learners passionate about space science, technology, research, and problem solving. We aim to collaborate, explore new ideas and develop creative solutions to real world challenges using Science and Technology, we welcome members with skills in programming, AIML, data analysis, electronics, design, research and creative thinking. Most importantly, we value teamwork, curiosity, dedication and a willingness to learn. Let's innovate together.
summary:
Project SYNEX is an Astronaut Health-Monitoring and Decision-Support System designed to support astronaut health monitoring during long-duration space missions. The project focuses on identifying potential health changes, providing evidence-informed recommendations, and tracking recovery through a structured monitoring workflow.

The system organises health monitoring into dedicated categories, including physical health, mental health, musculoskeletal health, neurological and vision health, immune and skin health, environmental health, and radiation monitoring. Its core prototype uses 11 selected input parameters, a personal baseline established during the first 14 days, and two separate assessment engines for health changes and radiation exposure.

A key feature is its closed-loop approach: Detect, Act, Verify, and Escalate. The proposed offline-first design aims to support monitoring even when communication with Earth is delayed or unavailable.

Project SYNEX is a proof of concept using synthetic and manually entered data, not a clinically validated medical device.
details: Project SYNEX is an astronaut health-monitoring system designed for long-duration space missions. It monitors 11 health and environmental parameters using two independent engines: Health Drift Monitoring and Radiation Exposure Monitoring. The system establishes a personal baseline over the first 14 days, identifies potential health changes, and provides recommendations through a DETECT → ACT → VERIFY → ESCALATE workflow. Its offline-first design aims to support health monitoring during communication delays. The project is a proof of concept using synthetic and manually entered data, not a clinically validated medical device.
